sets.context: Many teenagers now bring a smartphone to every lesson.

link.prompt: Where is the paragraph heading? Choose the linking word.

steps.prompt: Turn it into a view. Add a frame at the start.

steps.prompt: Say what the limit is for. Every option works — choose one.
steps.note: To + verb shows purpose. It adds a non-finite clause without adding a new subject.

sets.context: Supporters of homework believe it builds good study habits.

link.prompt: Where is the paragraph heading? Choose the linking word.

options.why: Furthermore adds a point on the same side. This sentence gives the opposite view.

steps.prompt: Add the result with an -ing form.

options.why: A past verb with no subject can’t join the sentence. Use -ing to show the result.

steps.prompt: Add the condition.

options.t: if it takes up every evening

steps.note: First conditional: if + present, with can or will in the main clause.

steps.prompt: Say which critics. Every option works — choose one.
steps.note: A defining clause tells you which critics, so it takes no commas.

sets.context: Tourism brings both money and problems to small towns.

steps.prompt: Give your own view.

options.why: Believe is a state verb, so it isn’t used in the continuous.
What means the thing that. Before a whole clause, use that.

steps.prompt: Open with a participle.

options.why: A past participle alone would mean I was considered. Use having + past participle.
